skill.author: browser-use

security_audit.summary: The audit confirms four medium-risk execution surfaces: documented heredoc workflows pass Python into the browser-use process for execution. Most other static detections are Markdown formatting, fixed commands, documentation links, or safe credential input. Semantic review also found anti-bot evasion guidance, automatic SSO behavior, and opt-in loading of unaudited domain instructions.

remediation.issue: The documented heredoc interface executes generated Python in the local browser-use process.
remediation.suggestion: Replace broad exec-based input with typed operations or a restricted sandbox, and require review before running generated Python.

remediation.issue: Cloud browser guidance recommends managed IPs and stealth settings to avoid anti-automation controls.
remediation.suggestion: Remove evasion guidance and require agents to respect site terms, captchas, access restrictions, and rate limits.

remediation.issue: Domain mode loads every matching local skill file without a stated trust or integrity boundary.
remediation.suggestion: Load only allowlisted, integrity-checked files and instruct agents to treat their contents as untrusted reference data.

remediation.issue: The workflow permits automatic SSO when Chrome already has an authenticated account.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user approval before starting SSO or creating any authenticated session, even when Chrome is already signed in.

semantic_findings.description: When domain skills are enabled, the agent must read every file in a host-specific directory. Modified files can inject unaudited instructions into browser tasks.

content.user_title: Automate Browser Tasks with Direct CDP Control
content.value_statement: Browser tasks often require reliable navigation, inspection, and interaction across dynamic pages. This skill controls Chrome through CDP for automation, extraction, testing, screenshots, and recordings.
actual_capabilities: Connect to local Chrome through CDP and run connection diagnostics.
Start isolated Browser Use cloud sessions for remote or parallel tasks.
Inspect accessibility trees, DOM content, page state, and element geometry.
Navigate tabs, click coordinates, wait for loads, and execute targeted page JavaScript.
Capture screenshots, traces, recordings, and videos using documented workflows.
Reference external Browser Harness guides for frames, downloads, uploads, scrolling, and other browser interactions.
limitations: Requires an installed browser-use harness and CDP-accessible Chrome or configured cloud access.
Local Chrome control requires the user to enable remote debugging and approve browser permission.
Cloud sessions require authentication, use third-party infrastructure, and may incur charges until stopped.
Does not guarantee access through captchas, rate limits, login walls, or site automation controls.

use_cases.title: Validate Web Journeys
use_cases.description: Exercise navigation and interface steps, verify page state, and capture evidence for failures.

use_cases.title: Collect Page Research
use_cases.description: Inspect permitted pages and extract focused information from accessibility or DOM content.

use_cases.title: Diagnose Browser Interfaces
use_cases.description: Inspect elements, frames, tabs, and loading behavior while reproducing application issues.

prompt_templates.title: Summarize a Page
prompt_templates.prompt: Open {url}, wait for loading, summarize the visible content, and report access or login barriers. Do not sign in.

prompt_templates.title: Perform a Verified Action
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect {url} with the accessibility tree. Find {element}, perform {action}, and verify the resulting page state. Ask before authentication.

prompt_templates.title: Test a Web Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Test {workflow} on {site}. Record each step and capture evidence for failures. Stop before purchases, submissions, authentication, or consent.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Sites in Isolated Sessions
prompt_templates.prompt: Use isolated sessions to compare {urls}. Extract {fields}, note discrepancies, preserve source pages, and request approval before closing billable sessions.

output_examples.input: Open example.com and summarize the page.
output_examples.output: The page loaded successfully. It shows the Example Domain heading, a short explanation, and a More Information link.

output_examples.input: Test the checkout flow until payment and report each result.
output: Product page loaded and the selected item entered the cart.
Cart quantity and subtotal matched the requested values.
Checkout required authentication, so testing stopped before sign-in or payment.

output_examples.input: Compare the visible pricing tiers on two approved product pages.
output: The first page displayed three public plans with monthly prices.
The second page displayed two public plans and required contact for enterprise pricing.
No account, form submission, or restricted page was used.

best_practices: Confirm the target pages, permitted actions, and stopping conditions before browser work.
Prefer accessibility and DOM inspection, then verify every interaction with focused page evidence.
Request approval before authentication, submissions, paid resources, or leaving remote sessions active.
anti_patterns: Do not bypass captchas, rate limits, access restrictions, or site automation controls.
Do not print API keys, passwords, cookies, tokens, or sensitive page content.
Do not rely only on screenshots when structured accessibility or DOM evidence is available.

faq.question: Does this skill require a browser installation?
faq.answer: Yes. Local use requires a compatible Chrome or Chromium browser with remote debugging enabled.

faq.question: Can it use a remote browser?
faq.answer: Yes. Browser Use cloud sessions support remote and parallel work, but they require authentication and may incur charges.

faq.question: Can it sign in to websites automatically?
faq.answer: Authentication is sensitive. The workflow should obtain approval before SSO and stop for passwords, MFA, consent, or ambiguous account selection.

faq.question: Can it capture recordings or videos?
faq.answer: Yes. Recording must be enabled or requested, and the exact recording path should be retained for later video creation.

faq.question: How does it find page elements?
faq.answer: It prefers the accessibility tree and DOM inspection. Screenshots are useful when layout, imagery, or canvas content matters.

faq.question: Does it bypass captchas or rate limits?
faq.answer: It should not bypass site controls. Stop when access restrictions appear and follow the site terms and user authorization.
